pitch_detail.notes: A single long linked lead up the widening crack along the upper edge of the first roof of the neighbouring route. Gear is plentiful, and there is a belay stance partway if the rope needs splitting. Easy angle, roughly 5.2.
Meet the neighbouring route at its second belay and take that route's third pitch: face holds up and right to a blank corner, then flakes back left to a high ledge with a slung block belay.
A very long traverse leftward across slabs, passing under one roof and over another. The features are excellent but protection is sparse. The rock can be wet in early season.
Angle up and left on a mossy slab to a belay just under the trees.
One last slab pitch up to a heather belay. Under dry conditions it is little more than a walk; wet slab was helped along with tree branches on the first ascent.

review.changed: Wrote 5 entries (p1-2 and p4-5 treated as linked leads) covering the 7 numbered pitches; no bolts, anchors or crux stated. No rappel stations listed.
review.other_findings: Stored pitches 6 vs 7 numbered pitches described (linked into 5 leads).

pitch_detail.notes: Layback the right-facing corner to a bolted anchor. This is the opening pitch and carries the first 5.10c grade.
Hand jams in a double crack, with a couple of 5.9 moves to reach Gecko Ledge.
A thin, tricky crack leads to a small ledge with a bolt, then a short vertical crack, a face and finally corner climbing. Full-value pitch with limited gear. Bolted belay.
Blocky chimney to a bolted anchor.

Strenuous offwidth, then an exposed bolt ladder over a huge roof; the ladder is reachy so bring aiders and expect to high-step. Either traverse an awkward slab or pendulum across to the crack, then climb to a bolted anchor. The second must lower out from the top bolt. Keep clear of the loose car-sized block.
A crack gives onto a groove with a couple of bolts; finish by moving rightward into the trees, where the belay is bolted.
Slab climbing with long gaps between protection, followed by a push through thick cedar to reach Petty Dwarf Crossing, where a bolted anchor waits.
Traverse far left along the ledge to a left-facing corner, then climb the bushy bulging corner up to a larger arching left-facing corner. Gear belay; watch for fire ants.

Continue left across runout slab past two bolts, a reachy move up a flake to a ledge, tree belay. Rappel from trees far right on this ledge on the way down. Details of this pitch are uncertain: the bolts were not found and it was bypassed with a runout 5.8 slab and cedar thrashing.
Easy unprotected groove.
Third-class scramble to the summit.

review.changed: Wrote 11 pitches from the per-pitch list; pitch 9 and the upper pitches flagged as uncertain by the text. No lengths stated. No rappel station list (just 60m raps down the route), so no rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: Follow the left-trending ramp to a V-shaped slot and a two-bolt anchor. One bolt and one piton on the way.
A beta-heavy crux with a bolt on the arete, easing off to a bolted anchor in a dish.
The line wanders. Aim for a left-facing corner about 30m up, passing a fixed pin, climb it, then go up a ramp right before returning left to a good ledge with a bolted belay.
Crack above the belay until you can step left over a ledge, then follow the crack toward a roof and build a gear anchor. Can be linked with the next pitch if rope drag allows.
The most continuous pitch. Lieback a crack with a few insecure moves, surmount the big roof on its left side, then make an exposed rightward traverse to a bolted anchor.
Two bolts protect a thin layback seam, then up and right through a steep flake past a fixed pin, two more bolts through a steep arch, and back left round an overhang to a bolted anchor.

One bolt covers a delicate slab, after which good gear protects the passage through the left part of a roof. Continue in the left-facing corner until it lies back, gaining the ridge under the summit, where a bolted anchor sits.

review.changed: Wrote all 7 pitches. Rappel text gives only a count and rope length (four 55m raps), not stations, so no rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: Rambling rock with a few interesting moves, about 8 draws. Belay at the chains on the grassy ledge.
Hard move right off the stance, then steady climbing the rest of the way; budget about 9 draws.

review.changed: Wrote 2 pitches; no lengths or bolt counts stated (draw counts only in notes). Rappel is with a 60m rope, no stations listed.

pitch_detail.notes: Start left of the fault; a few easy moves, then trend right to the anchor, whose chains show from below.
Scrambly off the belay, with a steeper step just under the anchor. Be careful if the heather step is wet.
Just a couple of moves from the station before easy slab. It combines readily with the pitch above.
Slab that gradually gets steeper. Returning onto the heather is the head game here. Afterwards, relocate the belay roughly 30m up and to the left.
Steep start, then a hard move left after the scrappy crux.
Fine climbing capped by a black roof; the move through it is the route's crux.

Angle up right toward the forest tunnel. Continue beyond the chain on the tree to the bolted anchor, unless drag from linking the previous two pitches forces a stop. Both descent lines work. Afterwards shift the belay roughly 40m up and left.
Great rock and position, with a few thin moves low down.
Thoughtful climbing on good rock.
Continuous climbing that bites near the top, more so when combined with the previous pitch. Afterwards, relocate the belay roughly 30m leftward.
Work leftward in an airy spot, then tackle steeper rock over an alcove. Manage rope drag.
Big step up from the stance, then a scramble over crumbly rock. Sharp edges sit close to the rappel start.

review.changed: Wrote all 12 pitches with grade and bolt counts. No rappel station list.

pitch_detail.notes: Bouldery start, then easy climbing to a large ledge left of the old adit. The next five bolts above are surprisingly steep, with the technical crux just under the anchor.
Weave left and right around a blunt prow; easier above.

review.changed: Wrote 2 pitches; text gives no grades, lengths or bolt counts per pitch.

pitch_detail.notes: Ledges lead up to a steeper headwall under a large flake; the crux is near the second bolt.
Steep flake leads to a small roof. Finding the concealed hold keeps it at 5.9; otherwise the large holds will pump you out.
Sustained, fun climbing on interesting rock.

review.changed: Wrote 3 pitches. Bolt counts not given (fewer than 12 per pitch). Rappel with a 60m rope, no stations.

pitch_detail.notes: A short scrambly pitch with about four bolts.
One move rated 5.7 or 5.8 right after the anchor, then it eases. Its anchor is also used by the neighbouring route Arrogant Frog.

review.changed: Wrote 2 pitches; P2 grade hedged in the text (5.7 or 5.8), wrote 5.7 and noted it. Bolt count only approximate so not stored.

pitch_detail.notes: Enter the moat and climb a left-facing corner or ramp on easy cracks to a ledge belay.
Up and right, then slightly back left into an open bay, with the gendarme visible above and right.
Cracks on either side get you started; the corner system on the right then continues up to a ledge giving a good belay.
Climb left of the gendarme in the right-hand crack until it ends at a small ledge. Bring wide gear if you prefer the left crack as an offwidth.
A short scramble relocates the belay to the upper left of the corner.
Enter a right-facing corner beside the spur and lieback it to a ledge, then scramble to a spot beneath a wide chimney.
Blocky chimney with its crux in the middle, then a hands-to-fingers crack on the right side to exit the chimney top.
Skirt around to the left, or take the short 5.10a hand crack in a deep corner, to reach gentler ground and a sandy ramp leading to a low corner.

Exit the corner leftward over poor rock, cross a slab to a ramp holding a left-facing corner, then gain a second ramp up and right, which has a gentle hand crack (staying far right is easier). A short finger-width traverse left reaches a gully, and a large protruding flake on its left side serves as the belay.
Up the gully, then left to a second gully (snow-filled in the account), scramble up loose blocks to the North Ridge. A steep wall variation at the gully mouth can be split in two to reduce drag.

review.changed: Wrote 10 entries (pitch 0 through 9) from a personal account; grades described as suggested. Some length ranges omitted.
review.other_findings: Stored pitches 9 vs 10 numbered including pitch 0; route grade 5.7 while text suggests 5.8 on pitches 5-6.

pitch_detail.notes: Climb up and left on a ramp to a sling belay at the middle of the published first pitch, rather than straight up.

Up a right-facing dihedral for 10m, swing left to a horizontal crack (use long slings), traverse 15m left to a blocky right-facing dihedral and climb it with marginal gear to the balcony. Two ropes are needed.
About 100m of walking left along the balcony.
Left-facing dihedral to a belay below the chimney roof.
The chimney roof; strenuous.
Loose, card-castle blocks; angle up and right so the belayer is out of the fall line.
Nice left-facing dihedral, though the account strayed right and ended on a ledge with two pitons. The bolt ladder is about 15m left.
Old bolt ladder with a few knifeblade-style pitons, then an offwidth above; large cams were helpful.
Long sustained left-facing dihedral with good stemming, the start of about 80m of crux climbing.
Continues the crux dihedral for another 20m or so, then easier right-trending ledges.
Right-trending ramp to a snow patch.
Up the corner to the Northeast ridge.
Simul-climb to the summit.

review.changed: Wrote 13 pitches from a personal account of one ascent; the account describes some variations off route.

pitch_detail.notes: Crack protected by two bolts plus gear. The hardest moves come close to the top of the crack.
Low-angle face climbing with one bolt plus gear, ending at a bushy tree ledge.
From the tree ledge, a mossy ramp to a bolt, then into a corner crack followed to the top.
An obvious bolt comes first, then wander rightward to a second, less visible bolt. Slab mixed with broken features, with gear only now and then.
Climb to a bolt, traverse left, continue up with gear where it can be found, then traverse left around a tree and step onto it to reach the wall.
Stay on the buttress crest directly to the anchor.
Continue up the buttress past two bolts.

review.changed: Wrote all 7 pitches. Descent is a mix of scrambling, a fixed rope and two rappels (30m first); not a full station list so no rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: Start up the slab left of the major chimney, make challenging moves across the gash to get under the crack, pull the small roof into the slot, then follow the obvious crack to a big ledge. The ledge can be wet early season.
Corner with a broken crack, with hard moves where you pull out above it; the rock is good. Several cracks then lead to a ledge littered with loose rock.
Blocky short ridge to the summit.

review.changed: Wrote 3 pitches. Descent raps from bolted anchors down the NE route; no station list.

pitch_detail.notes: Straight up a corner to the top of a ridge; a block at the top takes a sling.
A few metres of low 5th class to a wide ledge, then follow it right and around to the back of the peak.
Go directly up a corner, using a few hand-jam moves, to reach the summit block.

review.changed: Wrote 3 pitches. Descent: two 30m raps down the NE gully; not a station list.

pitch_detail.notes: Choose from several fist or wide cracks at the base of a pillar just up and right of the neighbouring arete; the leftmost corner has nice fists to fingers. Gear belay on a stance under double cracks.
Hands to fingers in double cracks, then into a higher dihedral and through a fourth-class section where the route meets the neighbouring route. Gear belay or bolted anchor.
Trend rightward to the big dihedral, work up its corner across a trough and then a hand-width crack. Build a gear belay beneath the lowest roof.
Cracks in the left wall get past the roof. Expect loose blocks, dirt and plants. Belay on gear, on the left wall under the top roof.
Either stay in the dihedral to where the corner system ends, or cross by ledges and cracks onto the left face and merge with the neighbouring routes last pitch beneath the summit block.

review.changed: Wrote all 5 pitches. Descent shares the neighbouring route (seven raps, single 60m rope) but no station list.

pitch_detail.notes: Short easy pitch on broken rock. Start with the 5.8 direct option: climb the triangle formed by two cracks into an alcove under flakes, move right and follow cracks and flakes to the ledge. Or traverse in from the left to avoid the 5.8 section.
Head left up cracks and belay under a notch leading to a ramp.
Up the notch with an awkward mantle onto the ramp, follow it to its end and belay.
Flakes toward the chimney; belay in an alcove.
Continue up the chimney to a belay in the notch between the two ears.
Cracks and ledges on the north side lead to the summit of the East Ear.

review.changed: Wrote 6 pitches matching the stored count; the route grade 5.8+ comes from the optional direct start. No rappel station list.

pitch_detail.notes: A gently angled crack slants toward the right end of a big roof; pass the roof on its right and keep following cracks until the approach ledge, where you belay.
Move up and rightward over the terrace for a brief pitch to a second grassy ledge, then walk right along it and belay under the pale clean wall that has a splitter crack.
Get onto the face crack dividing the pale wall and follow it up to a horizontal break, where you belay.
Crack in a left-facing corner past a small offwidth roof to a large flake pedestal. Belay there or continue up the crack on the left.
Use the left-hand crack over the pedestal heading for a roomy ledge. Halt before reaching it and belay at the horizontal crack that runs off rightward.
The mental crux: traverse right onto an airy face, continue right to a large sloping ledge and belay in the notch at its back.

A deep chimney-corner overhead, exiting right below a roof into the main chimney of the neighbouring route. Many loose blocks and chockstones make this risky for the belayer, so an alternative is to downclimb a short slab (about 10m) and belay inside that chimney.
Climb the airy chimney to the notch (60m on the alternate finish).

review.changed: Wrote all 8 pitches, including the alternate pitch 7-8 finish in notes.

pitch_detail.notes: Probably around 5.7; no clear line, follow the path of least resistance. Felt the dirtiest pitch of the route.
Includes a fun little 5.6 hand crack, ending in a sandy gully feature with a big ledge for the belay.
Look left for a chimney feature; going straight leads to black slabs.
Above the black slabs there is a small offwidth you could climb; most people instead trend right onto the ridge, which doubles as the descent, to a notch.
Face moves lead to an enjoyable 5.7 hand crack, then a tilted crack with tougher 5.9 climbing to the finish. Small pieces are welcome near the top.

review.changed: Wrote 5 pitches; text is loose on lengths and grades. An approach pitch (ramp or direct start of Ears Between) is not entered. Stored count 6 vs 5 described plus approach.

pitch_detail.notes: Begin at the low point of the face on cracks a few metres to the left of a roof, then angle rightward to the ledge that circles the face. Walking along that ledge reaches the same spot.
Short pitch above the ledge to a small terrace; shared with the neighbouring route Edwards-Neufeld.
Take cracks at the left side of the terrace to a pale, clean corner, then continue up the corner and a face crack to a horizontal break for the belay.
Continue above to a black ramp.
Follow the ramp to the base of an upper dihedral.
Climb the dihedral, which has an offwidth section, to a belay near its top. Loose rock, so keep the belayer clear of fall line.
Stemming and climbing for 30m on poor gear brings you to the shoulder not far under the top.

review.changed: Wrote all 7 pitches. Rappel is via bolted anchors atop the south summit; no full station list.

pitch_detail.notes: Optional lower pitch: move up right into a left-facing corner, follow twin cracks, and mantle onto the following grassy ledge.
Trend rightward into a low-angled left-facing dihedral, ending upward and right of the big boulder; a rappel sling is visible there.
Up the left-facing corner, transitioning into thinner cracks to the left, then trending left into rambling terrain with short hand and fist cracks to sling a horn below the roof block.
Head up right into the right-facing headwall. Going straight cuts rope drag; the other option drifts right past a further rappel sling and descends a slab to the ledge over the roof block.
From the belay move up, then down and left on hand and fist cracks into the gully. Easy to protect a second.
One move up and left of the belay, then continue on ramps to regain the ridge.
Scramble over boulders toward the upper left, ending at the foot of the middle tower.
Twin corner cracks, a touch wider than hands, lead to the summit. Feels secure and takes good gear.

review.changed: Wrote pitches 0 through 7. Account notes the climbers traversed off the main ridge line above pitch 3.

pitch_detail.notes: Starts with third-class scrambling, then a near-vertical thrash up exposed bushes to a ledge. A good boulder serves as a rappel anchor.
Leftward traverse with a few exposed 5th-class moves; not tricky.
A tricky friction step onto a smooth slab is the crux; sustained fourth class for about 20m follows, then easy ground to the summit.

review.changed: Wrote 3 pitches; grades not given per pitch. Descent is three short raps, no station detail.
